land.text: the Mongolian core of the Yuan (Shangdu, Yingchang, Karakorum), retained when the court left Dadu in September 1368

predecessors.note: Cliopatria keeps the Yuan Dynasty row to 1374 and draws this land in it; the Northern Yuan row starts in 1375.

land.text: the Mongolian steppe under Esen's Oirats, 9,639 of the Northern Yuan's last 9,642 cells

successors.note: Cliopatria draws the Mongol Khanate (mongol-khanate) over the same land from 1468; the page keeps one Northern Yuan to 1635.

capitals.name: Yingchang
capitals.note: Infobox 1369-1370. Coordinates approximate (Dalai Nor, Inner Mongolia); Yingchang is not in the gazetteer.

capitals.name: Karakorum
capitals.note: Infobox 1371-1388; the pages opened name no later seat, and the Yongle page has an Oirat leader install a puppet khan at Karakorum in 1412, so the dot stays to 1439.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1368-1374: Cliopatria's first Northern Yuan shape begins in 1375, but the page dates the Northern Yuan from 1368 ('fall of Dadu to Ming forces, September 1368'). Cliopatria's Yuan Dynasty row (1363-1374, 12.2 M km2) contains this whole shape (14,328 of its 14,329 cells) together with 20,913 cells that are Ming land from 1368, so the Yuan dossier should end the Chinese Yuan in 1368 and leave the Mongolian core to this one. The 1375 shape is used for 1368-1374.

correction.text: the 1375 shape (Mongolia, the north of Inner Mongolia and the Siberian margin) used for 1368-1374: the Yuan court's retreat from Dadu to Shangdu, Yingchang and Karakorum

keyframe_review.note: 3.44 M km2 for 1375-1401 (14,329 cells): the whole of Mongolia (Outer Mongolia 6,307 of 6,490 cells, the Orkhon Valley), 1,895 cells of Inner Mongolia, 732 of Dzungaria, 292 of Turfan-Hami, 388 of Manchuria and 4,853 of the Siberian margin to Lake Baikal. The page gives no area for these years; its only extent statement is for Dayan Khan's apogee (Siberian tundra and Lake Baikal, the Gobi, the Yellow River edge and the Ordos, Manchurian forests, the Altai). Frontier events that the shape does not show: the Ming sack of Karakorum in 1380 (about 70,000 captives, then withdrew), Naghachu's surrender in southern Manchuria in 1387-1388 and the Uriankhai Three Guards of the 1390s; the shape keeps 388 Manchurian cells and all of eastern Mongolia to 1439 (unverified: page budget).

2.29 M km2 for 1402-1414: 4,302 cells (1.15 M km2) fewer than 1375-1401, 3,352 of them inside the Four Oirats' first shape (western Mongolia, the Altai and the Dzungarian edge). The Oirats page: after the Yuan's expulsion the Oirats 'took power in the Altai region, northwest of Hami oasis, and then spread east, annexing territory held by the Eastern Mongols' (undated); the Northern Yuan page has the Oirats rising 'after the Uskhal defeat in 1388, becoming kingmakers'; the Yongle page has the Oirat leader Mahmud kill Bunyashiri in 1412 and install a puppet khan at Karakorum. The year 1402 is Cliopatria's (ledger, confidence 1).

2.18 M km2 for 1415-1421: 397 cells of the south-western edge (90-103 E, 41-51 N) pass to the Ming's 1415 shape. The Yongle page gives the 1414 campaign into Mongolia (a battle along the upper Tuul river, back in Beijing by August) and says 'No territory change is stated'; the step is Cliopatria's (ledger, confidence 1).

2.18 M km2 for 1422-1430, one cell different from 1415. The Yongle page has marches against the Eastern Mongols in 1422, 1423 and 1424 that 'achieved few tangible results' (the Northern Yuan page: against Arughtai in 1422 and 1423); no land changes.

2.18 M km2 for 1431-1439, identical to 1422. The Esen page: Toghon installed Taisun as a puppet Great Khan after Arughtai's death in 1434; Toghon died in 1438 and Esen 'inherited the title of taishi'. Cliopatria ends the row in 1439 and its Four Oirats shape of 1440 covers 9,639 of this shape's 9,642 cells.

ledger.note: September 1368: Toghon Temur flees Dadu for Shangdu as Ming forces approached, and the Yuan court continues on the steppe. Infobox 'Start: 1368 (fall of Dadu to Ming forces, September 1368)'; the page's 'Toghon Temur fled north to Shangdu from Dadu as Ming forces approached'. The land is the reading: the page names Shangdu, Yingchang and Karakorum, not a boundary.

region.text: the Mongolian core of the Yuan: Shangdu, Yingchang and the Mongolian plateau to Karakorum

ledger.note: 1369: the court moves from Shangdu to Yingchang. Infobox: 'Shangdu (1368-1369); Yingchang (1369-1370)'.

1370: the Ming take the Inner Mongolian capitals. Toghon Temur 'died in Yingchang in 1370. The Ming seized Yingchang shortly after'; the court retreats to Karakorum. Biligtu Khan's general Koke Temur 'defeated a Ming pursuit in 1372'; the Ming sacked Karakorum in 1380.

region.text: the Inner Mongolian steppe south of the Gobi inside the Northern Yuan's 1375 shape: Shangdu, Yingchang and the Ming frontier

ledger.note: 1371: the court settles at Karakorum. Infobox: 'Karakorum (1371-1388)'.

1388: the Yuan name is dropped. 'Jorightu Khan Yesuder took the throne in 1388 with Oirat support and dropped Han-style titles'; 'the Han-style Great Yuan name was dropped under Jorightu'. The page says 'Northern Yuan' is sometimes limited to 1368-1388.

18 May 1388: the Ming win at Buir Lake. 'Ming victory': General Lan Yu with about 150,000 soldiers found the Northern Yuan horde northeast of the lake and attacked it 'under darkness and a sandstorm'; about 80,000 Mongols were captured and Togus Temur 'was murdered by the Mongol chieftain Yesuder' on the Tula river. The Ming had sacked Karakorum in 1380 and received Naghachu's surrender in 1387.

region.text: the Inner Mongolian steppe south of the Gobi inside the Northern Yuan's 1375 shape: Shangdu, Yingchang and the Ming frontier

ledger.note: 1402: the western steppe passes to the Oirats on Cliopatria's map (4,302 cells fewer; 3,352 inside the Four Oirats' first shape). Page silent on the year: the Oirats 'took power in the Altai region ... and then spread east, annexing territory held by the Eastern Mongols' (undated).

region.text: the Altai, western Mongolia and Dzungarian edge that Cliopatria gives to the Four Oirats in 1402

ledger.note: 1415: 397 cells of the south-west edge pass to the Ming on Cliopatria's map. Page silent: the Yongle page's 1414 campaign has no territorial result ('No territory change is stated').

region.text: the south-western edge of the Mongolian plateau that Cliopatria gives to the Ming in 1415

ledger.note: 1439: Esen's Oirats take the khanate's lands. Toghon died in 1438 and Esen 'inherited the title of taishi', ruling through the Borjigin puppets Taisun (installed after Arughtai's death in 1434) and then Agbarjin (1452); in 1453 Esen declared himself Great Khan. The Borjigin khanship continues nominally to 1635 on the page; Cliopatria draws the land as the Four Oirats from 1440 and as the Mongol Khanate from 1468.

region.text: the khanate's lands, passing under the Oirats

wars.name: Ming-Northern Yuan wars of the Hongwu reign

zones.text: the Inner Mongolian steppe south of the Gobi inside the Northern Yuan's 1375 shape: Shangdu, Yingchang and the Ming frontier

wars.outcome: The Ming take Shangdu and Yingchang (1369-1370), Toghon Temur dies at Yingchang in 1370, Biligtu's general Koke Temur defeats a Ming pursuit in 1372, the Ming sack Karakorum in 1380 and withdraw, Naghachu surrenders in 1387 and the Ming win decisively at Buir Lake on 18 May 1388.
wars.note: The page gives the 1380 sack with about 70,000 captives; Xu Da (1370) and Lan Yu are not named on this page (Lan Yu is on the Buir Lake page).

wars.name: Ming conquest of Yunnan
wars.outcome: Yuan loyalists under Basalawarmi in Yunnan and Guizhou are defeated and killed. Yunnan is not part of Cliopatria's Northern Yuan shape, so no zone is given.
wars.note: The Northern Yuan page lists it among the Ming campaigns of '1381-82'.

wars.name: Battle of Buir Lake
wars.outcome: 18 May 1388: Ming victory; about 80,000 Mongols captured, Togus Temur murdered by Yesuder on the Tula river.

wars.name: Oirat ascendancy over the Mongol khanate
wars.outcome: After 1388 the Oirats become kingmakers, take the Altai and western Mongolia (Cliopatria 1402), install and depose Borjigin khans (Mahmud's puppet at Karakorum in 1412; Delbeg enthroned by Bahamu's Oirats in 1412) and under Esen (taishi from 1438) rule the whole steppe through Taisun Khan.
wars.note: The Oirats page is thin on dates; the Northern Yuan, Yongle and Esen pages supply them.

wars.name: Ming expeditions of the Yongle Emperor into Mongolia
wars.outcome: A Ming army is defeated in September 1409 (its commander Qiu Fu dies; 'Battle of Kherlen in 1409' on the Northern Yuan page); the emperor defeats Oljei Temur and Arughtai in March 1410, campaigns again in 1414, 1422, 1423 and 1424 (dying on 12 August 1424 at Yumuchuan). 'Achieved few tangible results': no territory changes; the Ming withdraw forward garrisons.

certainty.note: Steppe, Gobi and forest frontiers throughout, drawn approximate; the Ming wall frontier south of Shangdu is the firmest edge but no page gives a line.

notes:
Dates. The page dates the Northern Yuan 1368 (Dadu, September 1368) to 1635 (Ejei Khan's submission, February 1635; Ligdan Khan died in 1634) and says the name is 'sometimes limited to 1368-1388'. Cliopatria's row is 1375-1439, and the Yuan Dynasty row runs to 1374 over the same land (and over Ming China from 1368). This dossier starts in 1368 with a new keyframe (1368-1374) and ends in 1439 where Cliopatria's Four Oirats take over; the Mongol Khanate row (1468-1635, mongol-khanate, another batch) continues the Borjigin line, and the Esen page makes Esen the real ruler of Taisun Khan's realm from 1438 and Great Khan himself in 1453. Cliopatria's 'Golden Horde' shapes of 1547-1695 are the Mongol khanates of this line (see the golden-horde dossier). The Yuan dossier (ea-06) should end the Chinese Yuan in 1368 and not draw the Mongolian core in 1368-1374 as well.

Left out for want of a page: the Uriankhai Three Guards and Naghachu's southern Manchuria (the page: Naghachu 'invaded Liaodong in 1375 ... surrendered to the Ming in 1387-88'; Uriankhai 'surrendered to the Ming and were divided into the Three Guards' in the 1390s) are not turned into events because no page ties them to Cliopatria's shape or gives their land; Kara Del at Hami (founded by Gunashiri the year after 1388, lost to Turpan about 1517) and Basalawarmi's Liang principality in Yunnan (killed 1381-82) are states with no dossier. The 1415 step is Cliopatria's. The Yongle page does not name Arughtai for the 1422-1424 marches (the Northern Yuan page does for 1422 and 1423). Rulers: only the first three reigns (Toghon Temur 1368-1370, Biligtu 1370-1378, Uskhal 1378-1388) are on the infobox with years; the page gives no continuous list for 1388-1439, so no rulers are written.

Gazetteer names: Yingchang (place, Inner Mongolia, Dalai Nor; capital 1369-1370). Counterparts needing dossiers: Kara Del (Hami) 1389-c.1517; Naghachu's Liaodong 1375-1387; the Liang principality of Yunnan to 1382; the Uriankhai Three Guards. Page budget: five of five.
